gate_methodology.zero_lift_gate: primary, clean gate -- mirrors the DPW-8/HFCFDVW V2 case sheet's own mandatory check ('verify machine zero lift is computed on all grids'). Apples-to-apples: a symmetric body at alpha=0 has zero lift in BOTH inviscid theory (exact, by stagnation-point symmetry) and a mirror-symmetric viscous mesh (boundary-layer displacement is symmetric top/bottom), so CL~0 is a valid gate at any viscosity.
gate_methodology.surface_cp_gate: NOT graded as a strict PASS/FAIL against the inviscid exact curve, because a converged viscous RANS solution is not expected to reproduce the inviscid Cp exactly even at infinite grid resolution -- boundary-layer displacement and, especially, the finite-thickness wake behind a nominally-cusped trailing edge genuinely modify surface Cp versus potential flow. Graded instead on grid-convergence trend (does the CFD-vs-exact error shrink monotonically and sensibly with refinement, which is what would be expected of a correctly-behaving solver approaching the inviscid outer solution) -- observed: yes, ~3x reduction in mean/rms error from L1 to L3.
gate_methodology.cd_not_gated: exact inviscid Cd is 0 (d'Alembert); a nonzero viscous Cd (~3e-4, dropping with refinement as expected -- see L1 vs L3) is physically correct and is not comparable to the inviscid value, so it is reported but not gated.
gate_methodology.matching_artifact_caveat: Cp comparison uses nearest-neighbor matching of solver surface-sample points to a fixed 48/192-point theta grid; near the cusp (within ~15 deg) two adjacent sample points can be nearer to the same theta bin than to distinct ones (a real effect of the conformal map's compression toward zeta=+1), producing point-wise mismatches that are a matching artifact, not necessarily true solver error. 'far_from_cusp' stats exclude this window as a fairer comparison, following the F3 campaign's own precedent of reporting excl./incl. variants rather than picking the flattering one.
